newsitem.title: DUBAI: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC, MUSTER IN DUBAI OPEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC, MUSTER IN DUBAI OPEN FINAL.

text.p: Defending champion Goran Ivanisevic and second seed Thomas Muster both had to fight on Saturday to reach Sunday's final of the $1 million Dubai Open tennis tournament.
Croatian top seed Ivanisevic defeated unseeded Czech Jiri Novak 6-1 3-6 6-3 in his semifinal while Muster scrambled home against a rejuvenated Jim Courier 7-6 2-6 6-3 in a 2-1/2-hour marathon.
Muster and Courier exchanged seven service breaks in a row in the first set, which went to a tie-break which the Austrian won 7-3.
The pattern was similar in the second, in which there were four successive service breaks.
But former world number one Courier raised his game and reeled off five games in row to level the match.
Muster, frustrated by some line calls, held his nerve in the opening game of the deciding set after surviving three break points and moved into a 5-3 lead.
Courier saved two match points in the ninth game but Muster nailed the third.
"It was a tremendous match. When we kept breaking each other in the first set it looked more like a women's tennis match but then we returned very well and that led to the breaks," Muster said.
"I was a bit upset in the second because of some line calls. But I did not let that bother me in the decider.
"Jim is a great player. He's beaten me seven times and I needed to do something special to win, which eventually I did."
Earlier, Ivanisevic raced to a 3-0 lead against Novak, gained another break in the sixth game and took the first set barely raising a sweat.

But in the second set his serve seemed to desert him and the 67th-ranked Czech clawed his way back into the match. He broke the Croatian's serve to go 5-3 ahead and comfortably served out for the set.
Novak, who beat Australian Open finalist Carlos Moya in the first round, maintained the pressure in the deciding set.
But he failed to capitalise on two break points and it was Ivanisevic who made the decisive break to clinch the final set.
Ivanisevic admitted it had not been an easy win.
"Two easy misses by Novak in the seventh game of the third set swung the match in my favour," Ivanisevic, ranked second in the world, said.
"I struggled with my first serve but then Novak is not an easy player to beat. He hit the ball deep and hard."
